back: Plan Resource Management; Estimate Resources; Acquire Resources; Lead the Team; Monitor and Control Resourcing.
Human resources (the project team) and physical, material or virtual resources (equipment, materials, software, facilities).
A person with management authority over one or more resources, such as a functional manager. The project manager often has to negotiate with them.
The component of the project management plan that describes how project resources are acquired, allocated, monitored and controlled.
A document that sets the team's values, agreements and operating guidelines. Works best when the team develops it.
Expectations for acceptable behavior by team members, defined in the team charter. Everyone shares responsibility for following them.
A grid that shows the project resources assigned to each work package or activity.
Responsible (does the work), Accountable (answers for it), Consulted (gives input), Informed (is told the result).

front: How many people are accountable for one task in a RACI chart?
back: Exactly one.
A hierarchical representation of resources by category and type, such as labor, materials, equipment and supplies.
A hierarchy arranged by the organization's departments or teams, with the project work listed under each.
Shows the working days and shifts during which each specific resource is available.
Estimating the team resources and the type and quantities of physical resources needed. Outputs: resource requirements, basis of estimates, resource breakdown structure.
Resources determined in advance, for example people named in a proposal or needed for their particular expertise.
People with a shared goal who work with little or no face-to-face time. Wider choice of people and less travel; communication planning becomes more important.
Placing many or all of the most active team members in the same physical location to improve their ability to work as a team.
Guiding, developing and managing the team: improving competencies and interaction, giving feedback, resolving conflict. Older names: Develop Team, Manage Team.
Management: the means of meeting objectives (planning, coordinating, measuring). Leadership: people (influencing, motivating, listening, enabling).
Formal or informal assessments of the team's effectiveness as a whole: skills, teamwork, staff turnover, cohesiveness.
Ensuring physical and virtual resources are available as planned, comparing planned and actual use, and taking corrective action. Not about team members.
Forming, storming, norming, performing, adjourning.
Members meet and learn about the project and their roles. Independent and not yet open.
The team starts on the work and decisions; conflict appears as ideas and styles clash.
Members begin to work together, adjust their habits and learn to trust one another.
The team works as a well-organized, interdependent unit and handles issues smoothly.
The team completes the work and is released from the project.
Bringing in multiple viewpoints through open dialogue to reach consensus and commitment. Win-win. Usually the best technique.
Each side gives something up for partial satisfaction. Temporary or partial resolution; can be lose-lose.
Emphasizing areas of agreement and giving way to maintain harmony and relationships.
Pushing one viewpoint at the expense of others, usually from a power position. Win-lose. Suited to emergencies.
Retreating from the conflict or postponing it to be better prepared or to let others resolve it.
Scarce resources, scheduling priorities and personal work styles.
Hygiene (salary, policies, environment): cause dissatisfaction if missing, do not motivate. Motivational (achievement, growth, advancement): create satisfaction.

front: McGregor: Theory X vs Theory Y
back: X: people work only for income and need top-down supervision. Y: people are motivated to do good work and respond to coaching.
People are driven by needs for achievement, power and affiliation.
Autonomy, mastery and purpose.
From the bottom: physiological, safety, social, esteem, self-actualization.
A bar chart of the time a resource is scheduled to work in each period. A bar above availability shows an over-allocation.
A documented list of the team members, their project roles and how to reach them.
